title: Mirai_Botnet_Investigation_b72
description: Investigate and mitigate Mirai botnet activity targeting IoT devices.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. The service can be found by listing systemd timers with the command 'systemctl list-timers'.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is named 'malicious-timer.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. The service can be found by listing systemd timers with the command 'systemctl list-timers'.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be related to network diagnostics or probes. The service is named 'flood-timer.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be related to network diagnostics or probes.

levels.title: Determine Service Persistence
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. The timer unit can be found by listing systemd timers with the command 'systemctl list-timers'.
levels.solution: Look for systemd timer units that are associated with the suspicious service identified in the previous tasks. The timer unit is named 'malicious-timer.service'.
